newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso kept steady by C. Bank in edgy mkt.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso kept steady by C. Bank in edgy mkt.

text.p: In an edgy market, the Philippine peso was kept steady on Friday by the Philippine Central Bank which unloaded $111.5 million, dealers said.
The peso closed unchanged at 26.37, with volume higher at $178.1 million from $153.5 million.
"Banks are cautious because of the continuing talk the Philippines might become another Thailand," a foreign bank dealer said.
Concerns were raised that Philippine banks may suffer the same fate as Thailand if the property sector goes through a downturn.
The Philippine equities market had been battered this month as a result of these concerns, and which may cause dollar outflows, dealers said.
A second dealer said the news of financial troubles at a small thrift bank, Monte de Piedad and Savings Bank, sent ripples of concerns among investors.
"It has eroded investor confidence," a dealer said, which led banks to be cautious and buy dollars.
The government has dismissed it as an isolated case.
On Friday, traders said the peso could weaken but thatwill depend on how determined the Central Bank is to support the local currency.
